'''Burton S. "Burt" Kaliski, Jr.''' is a cryptographer, who is currently the [[chief technology officer]] (CTO) and senior vice president at [[Verisign]].<ref name="vrsnbio">[http://www.verisigninc.com/en_US/news-events/press-room/executive-bios/burt-kaliski/index.xhtml Dr. Burt Kaliski Jr., Verisign Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer]</ref> Before joining Verisign in 2011, he was the founding director of the EMC Innovation Network at [[EMC Corporation]] since its 2006 acquisition of [[RSA Security]] where he was Chief Scientist for RSA Laboratories. His notable work includes the development of such [[public key cryptography]] standards as [[PKCS]]<ref name="pkcs">[http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2315 PKCS #7: Cryptographic Message Syntax (RFC2315)]</ref> and [[IEEE P1363]],<ref name="ieeep1363">{{Cite web |url=http://grouper.ieee.org/groups/1363/passwdPK/index.html |title=Ford and Kaliski, IEEE P1363.2: Password-Based Public-Key Cryptography |access-date=2014-01-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019053133/http://grouper.ieee.org/groups/1363/passwdPK/index.html |archive-date=2013-10-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the extension of [[linear cryptanalysis]] to use multiple approximations, and the design of the [[block cipher]] [[Crab (cipher)|Crab]].

Kaliski received his B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. degrees in computer science from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], where his research was on cryptography.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|98549}}</ref> He was a visiting assistant professor of computer engineering at [[Rochester Institute of Technology]] before joining RSA Security.<ref name="RSABIO">[http://www.rsasecurity.com/rsalabs/node.asp?id=2017 Bio at RSA Laboratories] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061230131211/http://www.rsasecurity.com/rsalabs/node.asp?id=2017 |date=December 30, 2006 }}</ref>

He was also a guest professor and member of the international advisory board of [[Peking University]],  School of Software and Microelectronics.<ref name="RSABIO"/>
